---
title: "Sample-path bounds"
---

## Motivation

In the previous lectures, we have obtained bounds on policy error, value error, and model approximation error in terms of the sup-norm. In this lecture, we will develop sample path based bounds which are tighter. For simplicity, we reuse some of the symbols from the previous lectures, but their meanings are different.

## Model approximation (Take 3)

### One step error propagation

Recall that the **environment operator** $\ENV_t \colon \ALPHABET V \to \ALPHABET Q$ includes both the cost and the transition:
$$
  [\ENV_t v](s,a)
  = c_t(s,a) + \sum_{s' \in \ALPHABET S} P_t(s' \mid s,a) v(s').
$$
Define the **dynamics operator** $\DYNAMICS_t \colon \ALPHABET V \to \ALPHABET Q$ to be the transition part alone:
$$
  [\DYNAMICS_t v](s,a) 
  = \sum_{s' \in \ALPHABET S} P_t(s' \mid s,a) v(s').
$$
Thus $\ENV_t v = c_t + \DYNAMICS_t v$. As before, the mismatch is $\MISMATCH_t v = \ENV_t v - \hat \ENV_t v$.

:::{#lem-model-diff}

For any $v, \hat v \in \ALPHABET V$,
$$
  \ENV_t v - \ENV_t \hat v
  = \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v - \hat v \bigr].
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

The cost terms cancel:
\begin{align*}
  \ENV_t v - \ENV_t \hat v
  &= \bigl(c_t + \DYNAMICS_t v\bigr)
  - \bigl(c_t + \DYNAMICS_t \hat v\bigr)
  = \DYNAMICS_t v - \DYNAMICS_t \hat v
  = \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v - \hat v \bigr],
\end{align*}
where the last step uses linearity of $\DYNAMICS_t$.
:::

:::{#lem-one-step-signed}
#### One step error propagation

Given $v_{t+1}, \hat v_{t+1} \in \ALPHABET V$, define $q_t = \ENV_t v_{t+1}$ and $\hat q_t = \hat \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}$. Then
$$
  q_t - \hat q_t
  = \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \bigl[
    \ENV_t v_{t+1} - \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  = \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v_{t+1} - \hat v_{t+1} \bigr].
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Consider
\begin{align*}
  q_t - \hat q_t
  &= \ENV_t v_{t+1} - \hat \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \\
  &= \bigl[
    \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1} - \hat \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  + \bigl[
    \ENV_t v_{t+1} - \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  \\
  &= \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \bigl[
    \ENV_t v_{t+1} - \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  \\
  &= \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v_{t+1} - \hat v_{t+1} \bigr],
\end{align*}
where the third equality uses the definition of $\MISMATCH_t$ and the last equality uses @lem-model-diff.
:::

### Policy error

:::{#prp-policy-error-signed}
#### Policy error

For any policy $π = (π_1, \dots, π_T)$, define the policy errors
$$
  α^π_t(s)
  \coloneqq V^π_t(s) - \hat V^π_t(s),
  \qquad
  β^π_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq Q^π_t(s,a) - \hat Q^π_t(s,a),
$$
with the convention $α^π_{T+1} ≡ 0$. Then, for any $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$,
\begin{align*}
  β^π_t
  &= \MISMATCH_t \hat V^π_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^π_{t+1},
  \\
  α^π_t
  &= \ALPHABET T^{π_t} β^π_t.
\end{align*}
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Recall that
$$
  Q^π_t = \ENV_t V^π_{t+1},
  \quad
  \hat Q^π_t = \hat \ENV_t \hat V^π_{t+1},
$$
and $V^π_t = \ALPHABET T^{π_t} Q^π_t$, $\hat V^π_t = \ALPHABET T^{π_t} \hat Q^π_t$. From @lem-one-step-signed with $v_{t+1} = V^π_{t+1}$ and $\hat v_{t+1} = \hat V^π_{t+1}$,
$$
  β^π_t
  = Q^π_t - \hat Q^π_t
  = \MISMATCH_t \hat V^π_{t+1} + \DYNAMICS_t α^π_{t+1}.
$$
Since $\ALPHABET T^{π_t}$ is linear,
$$
  α^π_t
  = V^π_t - \hat V^π_t
  = \ALPHABET T^{π_t} Q^π_t - \ALPHABET T^{π_t} \hat Q^π_t
  = \ALPHABET T^{π_t} β^π_t.
$$
:::

### Value error

Similar to the above, we can also compare the optimal value functions of the true and approximate models.

:::{#prp-value-error-signed}
#### Value error

Define the value errors
$$
  α^\star_t(s)
  \coloneqq V^\star_t(s) - \hat V^\star_t(s),
  \qquad
  β^\star_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq Q^\star_t(s,a) - \hat Q^\star_t(s,a),
$$
with the convention $α^\star_{T+1} ≡ 0$. Then, for any $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$,
\begin{align*}
  β^\star_t
  &= \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^\star_{t+1},
  \\
  \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^\star_t
  &\le α^\star_t
  \le \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} β^\star_t.
\end{align*}
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Recall that
$$
  Q^\star_t = \ENV_t V^\star_{t+1},
  \quad
  \hat Q^\star_t = \hat \ENV_t \hat V^\star_{t+1},
$$
and $V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star Q^\star_t$, $\hat V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star \hat Q^\star_t$. From @lem-one-step-signed with $v_{t+1} = V^\star_{t+1}$ and $\hat v_{t+1} = \hat V^\star_{t+1}$,
$$
  β^\star_t
  = Q^\star_t - \hat Q^\star_t
  = \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1} + \DYNAMICS_t α^\star_{t+1}.
$$

The sandwich for $α^\star_t$ uses the two optimality properties, one at a time.

*Upper bound.* By optimality of $\hat π^\star_t$ on the approximate side, $\hat V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} \hat Q^\star_t$, while on the true side $V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star Q^\star_t \le \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} Q^\star_t$. Therefore
$$
  α^\star_t
  = V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t
  \le \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} Q^\star_t - \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} \hat Q^\star_t
  = \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} β^\star_t.
$$

*Lower bound.* By optimality of $π^\star_t$ on the true side, $V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} Q^\star_t$, while on the approximate side $\hat V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star \hat Q^\star_t \le \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} \hat Q^\star_t$. Therefore
$$
  α^\star_t
  = V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t
  \ge \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} Q^\star_t - \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} \hat Q^\star_t
  = \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^\star_t.
$$
:::

Unfortunately, the result of @prp-value-error-signed is uncomputable because we do not know the exact value of $α^\star_t$. However, as we explain below, it can be used to obtain model approximation error bounds by upper and lower bounding $\alpha^\star_t$.

### Model approximation bounds

As in the sup-norm case, the key idea is that
$$
  0 \le V^{\hat \pi^\star}_t - V^\star_t
  \le \bigl[\hat V^{\hat \pi^\star}_t - V^{\hat \pi^\star}_t \bigr]
    - \bigl[ V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t \bigr].
$$
So, we can take an upper bound on the first term and a lower bound on the second term to get a bound on the model error. We can get these (possibly loose) upper and lower bounds on $α^{\hat π^\star}$ and $α^\star$ by finding $(α^+, β^+)$ and $(α^-, β^-)$ that obey the same recursions but with inequalities instead of equalities.

:::{#thm-signed-sample-path}
#### Signed sample-path bound

Suppose that for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ there exist functions $α^+_t, α^-_t \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals$ and $β^+_t, β^-_t \colon \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A \to \reals$ such that
$$
  β^-_T \le \MISMATCH_T \hat V^\star_{T+1} \le β^+_T,
$$
and for $t < T$,
\begin{align*}
  β^-_t
  &\le \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1},
  \\
  α^-_t
  &\le \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^-_t,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
  β^+_t
  &\ge \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^+_{t+1},
  \\
  α^+_t
  &\ge \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} β^+_t.
\end{align*}
Then, for all $t$,
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t
  \le α^+_t - α^-_t.
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

The recursions for the upper bound and the lower bound are similar to the recursions for exact policy and value errors in @prp-policy-error-signed (specialized to $\hat π^\star$) and @prp-value-error-signed, with equalities replaced by inequalities. Therefore, a backward induction argument shows that $α^+_t$ is an upper bound on $α^{\hat π^\star}_t = V^{\hat π^\star}_t - \hat V^\star_t$ and $α^-_t$ is a lower bound on $α^\star_t = V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t$. Combining the two inequalities then gives
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t
  = α^{\hat π^\star}_t - α^\star_t
  \le α^+_t - α^-_t.
$$
:::

A concrete construction that uses the best upper bound and relaxes the lower bound (so that we don't need the knowledge of $π^\star$) is
\begin{align*}
  α^+_t
  &= \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t}\bigl(
    \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
    + \DYNAMICS_t α^+_{t+1}
  \bigr),
  \\
  α^-_t(s)
  &= \min_{a \in \ALPHABET C_t(s)}
  \Bigl[
    \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
    + \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1}
  \Bigr](s,a),
\end{align*}
where $\ALPHABET C_t(s) \subseteq \ALPHABET A$ is any set guaranteed to contain $π^\star_t(s)$ (for example $\ALPHABET C_t(s) = \ALPHABET A$, in which case $α^-_t = \ALPHABET T^\star\bigl(\MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1} + \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1}\bigr)$, or a structural candidate set that does not require computing $π^\star$ explicitly). @thm-signed-sample-path then guarantees
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t
  \le α^+_t - α^-_t.
$$

### Symmetric bounds

The above bound requires separately keeping track of an upper and lower bound. We can get symmetric upper and lower bounds by taking absolute values.

:::{#thm-abs-sample-path}
#### Absolute-value sample-path bound

Suppose that for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ there exist functions $α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals_{\ge 0}$ and $β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \colon \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A \to \reals_{\ge 0}$ such that
$$
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_T \ge \ABS{\MISMATCH_T \hat V^\star_{T+1}},
$$
and for $t < T$,
$$
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \ge \ABS{\MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^{\mathrm{abs}}_{t+1},
$$
and for all $t$,
$$
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \ge \max\Bigl\{
    \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,\;
    \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \Bigr\},
$$
where absolute values of $Q$-functions are pointwise. Then the policy $\hat π^\star$ satisfies, for all $t$,
$$
  \ABS{V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t}
  \le 2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t.
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Choose the upper and lower bounds
$$
  α^+_t = α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,
  \quad
  α^-_t = -α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,
  \quad
  β^+_t = β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,
  \quad
  β^-_t = -β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t.
$$
These satisfy the hypotheses of @thm-signed-sample-path, so
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t
  \le α^+_t - α^-_t
  = 2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t.
$$
For the matching lower side, optimality of $V^\star$ yields $V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t \ge 0 \ge -2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t$ because $α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \ge 0$. Combining the two inequalities gives the claim.
:::

A feasible (but state-independent) choice is
$$
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \equiv \sum_{\tau=t}^{T} \NORM{\MISMATCH_\tau \hat V^\star_{\tau+1}},
  \qquad
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \equiv \NORM{\MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^{\mathrm{abs}}_{t+1}.
$$
For this choice, @thm-abs-sample-path recovers the factor-of-two model-approximation bound from the model-approximation lecture:
$$
  \NORM{V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t}
  \le 2 \sum_{\tau=t}^{T} \NORM{\MISMATCH_\tau \hat V^\star_{\tau+1}}.
$$

## Computing the bounds

One difficulty in applying @thm-signed-sample-path is that the upper and lower bound recursions propagate with the true dynamics $\DYNAMICS_t$. Moreover, computing the mismatch $\MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}$ requires the true model.

In applications where $P_t$ is unknown or inconvenient to evaluate, we can obtain coarser bounds that use only the approximate model, at the price of an additional IPM penalty. Write $\hat \DYNAMICS_t$ for the dynamics operator of $\widehat{\ALPHABET M}$, so $[\hat \DYNAMICS_t v](s,a) = \sum_{s'} \hat P_t(s'\mid s,a)\, v(s')$.

Let $\def\F{\mathfrak{F}}\F$ be a (maximal) generator as in the model-approximation lecture, with IPM $d_{\F}$ and Minkowski functional $ρ_{\F}$. Suppose we are given $ε^{+}_t, ε^{-}_t \in \ALPHABET Q$ with
$$
  ε^{-}_t \le c_t - \hat c_t \le ε^{+}_t,
$$
and define $δ_t \in \ALPHABET Q$ by
$$
  δ_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq d_{\F}\bigl(P_t(\cdot \mid s,a), \hat P_t(\cdot \mid s,a)\bigr).
$$
(Here and below, products such as $δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(v)$ are pointwise.) The defining IPM inequality then yields, for any $v \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals$,
$$
  \ABS{\DYNAMICS_t v - \hat \DYNAMICS_t v}
  \le δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(v),
$$
or equivalently
$$
  \hat \DYNAMICS_t v - δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(v)
  \le \DYNAMICS_t v
  \le \hat \DYNAMICS_t v + δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(v).
$$
Applying this to $v = \hat V^\star_{t+1}$ and using $\MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1} = (c_t - \hat c_t) + (\DYNAMICS_t - \hat \DYNAMICS_t)\hat V^\star_{t+1}$ also bounds the one-step mismatch:
$$
  ε^{-}_t - δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})
  \le \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  \le ε^{+}_t + δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1}).
$$

Thus both the mismatch and the true dynamics can be replaced by approximate-model operators plus or minus an IPM correction. In particular, the recursions of @thm-signed-sample-path are implied by
\begin{align*}
  β^-_t
  &\le ε^{-}_t - δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})
  + \hat \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1}
  - δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(α^-_{t+1}),
  \\
  α^-_t
  &\le \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^-_t,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
  β^+_t
  &\ge ε^{+}_t + δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})
  + \hat \DYNAMICS_t α^+_{t+1}
  + δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(α^+_{t+1}),
  \\
  α^+_t
  &\ge \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} β^+_t.
\end{align*}
The resulting bounds are typically looser than those built from $\DYNAMICS_t$, but they are computable from the approximate model together with model error $(ε^\pm_t,δ_t)$.

## Model approximation with state abstraction (Take 4)

We now redo the sample-path bounds when the true model $\ALPHABET M = \langle \ALPHABET S, \ALPHABET A, P, c, T \rangle$ and the approximate model $\widehat {\ALPHABET M} = \langle \hat {\ALPHABET S}, \ALPHABET A, \hat P, \hat c, T \rangle$ live on different state spaces, related by a surjective abstraction $φ \colon \ALPHABET S \to \hat {\ALPHABET S}$. As in the state-abstraction lecture, we **lift** any $\hat f$ on $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$ to $\hat f \circ φ$ on $\ALPHABET S$, write $\hat π \circ φ$ for the lift of a policy $\hat π$ on $\widehat {\ALPHABET M}$, and use $(\hat q \circ φ)(s,a) \coloneqq \hat q(φ(s),a)$ for $\hat q \in \hat {\ALPHABET Q}$. 

The pointwise arguments carry over verbatim; the only change is that every comparison is between a function on $\ALPHABET S$ and the lift of a function on $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$. The details below are just for the sake of completeness.

### One step error propagation

Since the two models have different state spaces, we use the **mismatch operator** $\hat \MISMATCH_t \colon \hat {\ALPHABET V} \to \ALPHABET Q$ from the state-abstraction lecture: for $\hat v \in \hat {\ALPHABET V}$,
$$
  \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat v
  = \ENV_t (\hat v \circ φ) - (\hat \ENV_t \hat v) \circ φ.
$$
The dynamics operator $\DYNAMICS_t \colon \ALPHABET V \to \ALPHABET Q$ is that of the true model, exactly as before.

:::{#lem-one-step-signed-abstract}
#### One step error propagation

Given $v_{t+1} \in \ALPHABET V$ and $\hat v_{t+1} \in \hat {\ALPHABET V}$, define $q_t = \ENV_t v_{t+1}$ and $\hat q_t = \hat \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}$. Then
$$
  q_t - \hat q_t \circ φ
  = \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v_{t+1} - \hat v_{t+1} \circ φ \bigr].
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Add and subtract $\ENV_t(\hat v_{t+1} \circ φ)$:
\begin{align*}
  q_t - \hat q_t \circ φ
  &= \bigl[
    \ENV_t(\hat v_{t+1} \circ φ) - (\hat \ENV_t \hat v_{t+1}) \circ φ
  \bigr]
  + \bigl[
    \ENV_t v_{t+1} - \ENV_t(\hat v_{t+1} \circ φ)
  \bigr]
  \\
  &= \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v_{t+1} - \hat v_{t+1} \circ φ \bigr],
\end{align*}
where the last step uses the definition of $\hat \MISMATCH_t$ and @lem-model-diff.
:::

### Policy error

:::{#prp-policy-error-signed-abstract}
#### Policy error

For any policy $\hat π = (\hat π_1, \dots, \hat π_T)$ on $\widehat {\ALPHABET M}$, define the policy errors
$$
  α^{\hat π}_t(s)
  \coloneqq V^{\hat π \circ φ}_t(s) - \hat V^{\hat π}_t(φ(s)),
  \qquad
  β^{\hat π}_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq Q^{\hat π \circ φ}_t(s,a) - \hat Q^{\hat π}_t(φ(s),a),
$$
with the convention $α^{\hat π}_{T+1} ≡ 0$. Then, for any $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$,
\begin{align*}
  β^{\hat π}_t
  &= \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^{\hat π}_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^{\hat π}_{t+1},
  \\
  α^{\hat π}_t
  &= \ALPHABET T^{\hat π_t \circ φ} β^{\hat π}_t.
\end{align*}
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Recall that $Q^{\hat π \circ φ}_t = \ENV_t V^{\hat π \circ φ}_{t+1}$ and $\hat Q^{\hat π}_t = \hat \ENV_t \hat V^{\hat π}_{t+1}$. Applying @lem-one-step-signed-abstract with $v_{t+1} = V^{\hat π \circ φ}_{t+1}$ and $\hat v_{t+1} = \hat V^{\hat π}_{t+1}$,
$$
  β^{\hat π}_t
  = Q^{\hat π \circ φ}_t - \hat Q^{\hat π}_t \circ φ
  = \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^{\hat π}_{t+1} + \DYNAMICS_t α^{\hat π}_{t+1}.
$$
Since $V^{\hat π \circ φ}_t = \ALPHABET T^{\hat π_t \circ φ} Q^{\hat π \circ φ}_t$ and $\hat V^{\hat π}_t \circ φ = \ALPHABET T^{\hat π_t \circ φ}(\hat Q^{\hat π}_t \circ φ)$, linearity of $\ALPHABET T^{\hat π_t \circ φ}$ gives
$$
  α^{\hat π}_t
  = V^{\hat π \circ φ}_t - \hat V^{\hat π}_t \circ φ
  = \ALPHABET T^{\hat π_t \circ φ} β^{\hat π}_t.
$$
:::

### Value error

:::{#prp-value-error-signed-abstract}
#### Value error

Define the value errors
$$
  α^\star_t(s)
  \coloneqq V^\star_t(s) - \hat V^\star_t(φ(s)),
  \qquad
  β^\star_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq Q^\star_t(s,a) - \hat Q^\star_t(φ(s),a),
$$
with the convention $α^\star_{T+1} ≡ 0$. Then, for any $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$,
\begin{align*}
  β^\star_t
  &= \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^\star_{t+1},
  \\
  \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^\star_t
  &\le α^\star_t
  \le \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ} β^\star_t.
\end{align*}
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Applying @lem-one-step-signed-abstract with $v_{t+1} = V^\star_{t+1}$ and $\hat v_{t+1} = \hat V^\star_{t+1}$ gives $β^\star_t = \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1} + \DYNAMICS_t α^\star_{t+1}$. For the sandwich we use the two optimality properties, one at a time.

*Upper bound.* By optimality of $\hat π^\star_t$ on the approximate side, $\hat V^\star_t \circ φ = \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ}(\hat Q^\star_t \circ φ)$, while on the true side $V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star Q^\star_t \le \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ} Q^\star_t$. Therefore
$$
  α^\star_t
  = V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t \circ φ
  \le \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ} β^\star_t.
$$

*Lower bound.* By optimality of $π^\star_t$ on the true side, $V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} Q^\star_t$, while on the approximate side $\hat V^\star_t \circ φ = \ALPHABET T^\star(\hat Q^\star_t \circ φ) \le \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t}(\hat Q^\star_t \circ φ)$. Therefore
$$
  α^\star_t
  = V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t \circ φ
  \ge \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^\star_t.
$$
:::

### Model approximation bounds

As in the MDP case, optimality of $V^\star$ gives $V^{\hat π^\star \circ φ}_t \ge V^\star_t$, and since $\hat V^{\hat π^\star} = \hat V^\star$ (so $\hat V^{\hat π^\star}_t \circ φ = \hat V^\star_t \circ φ$),
$$
  0
  \le V^{\hat π^\star \circ φ}_t - V^\star_t
  = α^{\hat π^\star}_t - α^\star_t.
$$
As before, we bound the right-hand side by finding $(α^+, β^+)$ and $(α^-, β^-)$ that obey the same recursions with inequalities instead of equalities.

:::{#thm-signed-sample-path-abstract}
#### Signed sample-path bound

Suppose that for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ there exist functions $α^+_t, α^-_t \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals$ and $β^+_t, β^-_t \colon \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A \to \reals$ such that
$$
  β^-_T \le \hat \MISMATCH_T \hat V^\star_{T+1} \le β^+_T,
$$
and for $t < T$,
\begin{align*}
  β^-_t
  &\le \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1},
  \\
  α^-_t
  &\le \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^-_t,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
  β^+_t
  &\ge \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^+_{t+1},
  \\
  α^+_t
  &\ge \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ} β^+_t.
\end{align*}
Then, for all $t$,
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star \circ φ}_t - V^\star_t
  \le α^+_t - α^-_t.
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

As in @thm-signed-sample-path, a backward induction with @prp-policy-error-signed-abstract (for $\hat π^\star$) and @prp-value-error-signed-abstract shows that $α^+_t$ upper-bounds $α^{\hat π^\star}_t$ and $α^-_t$ lower-bounds $α^\star_t$. Combining the two,
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star \circ φ}_t - V^\star_t
  = α^{\hat π^\star}_t - α^\star_t
  \le α^+_t - α^-_t.
$$
:::

A concrete construction that uses the best upper bound and relaxes the lower bound (so that we don't need the knowledge of $π^\star$) is
\begin{align*}
  α^+_t
  &= \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ}\bigl(
    \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
    + \DYNAMICS_t α^+_{t+1}
  \bigr),
  \\
  α^-_t(s)
  &= \min_{a \in \ALPHABET C_t(s)}
  \Bigl[
    \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
    + \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1}
  \Bigr](s,a),
\end{align*}
where $\ALPHABET C_t(s) \subseteq \ALPHABET A$ is any set guaranteed to contain $π^\star_t(s)$ (for example $\ALPHABET C_t(s) = \ALPHABET A$, in which case $α^-_t = \ALPHABET T^\star\bigl(\hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1} + \DYNAMICS_t α^-_{t+1}\bigr)$).

### Symmetric bounds

Taking absolute values gives a symmetric bound, exactly as in @thm-abs-sample-path.

:::{#thm-abs-sample-path-abstract}
#### Absolute-value sample-path bound

Suppose that for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ there exist functions $α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals_{\ge 0}$ and $β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \colon \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A \to \reals_{\ge 0}$ such that
$$
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_T \ge \ABS{\hat \MISMATCH_T \hat V^\star_{T+1}},
$$
and for $t < T$,
$$
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \ge \ABS{\hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}}
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^{\mathrm{abs}}_{t+1},
$$
and for all $t$,
$$
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \ge \max\Bigl\{
    \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,\;
    \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ} β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \Bigr\},
$$
where absolute values of $Q$-functions are pointwise. Then the lifted policy $\hat π^\star \circ φ$ satisfies, for all $t$,
$$
  \ABS{V^{\hat π^\star \circ φ}_t - V^\star_t}
  \le 2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t.
$$
:::

The proof is identical to that of @thm-abs-sample-path, with $\hat π^\star_t$ replaced by $\hat π^\star_t \circ φ$. As before, the state-independent choice
$$
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t
  \equiv \sum_{\tau=t}^{T} \NORM{\hat \MISMATCH_\tau \hat V^\star_{\tau+1}}
$$
recovers the factor-of-two model-approximation bound of the state-abstraction lecture.

### Computing the bounds

As before, the bound of @thm-signed-sample-path-abstract is not directly computable: the recursions use the true dynamics $\DYNAMICS_t$, and the mismatch $\hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}$ depends on the true model. We obtain coarser bounds that live entirely on $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$. Write $\hat \DYNAMICS_t \colon \hat {\ALPHABET V} \to \hat {\ALPHABET Q}$ for the dynamics of $\widehat{\ALPHABET M}$.

Let $\F$ be as above, and write $P_{φ,t}$ for the pushed-forward kernel
$$
  P_{φ,t}(\hat s' \mid s,a)
  \coloneqq P_t\bigl(φ^{-1}(\hat s') \mid s,a\bigr).
$$
Suppose we are given $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$-measurable cost bounds $\hat ε^{+}_t, \hat ε^{-}_t \in \hat {\ALPHABET Q}$ with
$$
  \hat ε^{-}_t \circ φ
  \le c_t - \hat c_t \circ φ
  \le \hat ε^{+}_t \circ φ,
$$
and a $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$-measurable transition discrepancy $\hat δ_t \in \hat {\ALPHABET Q}$ with
$$
  d_{\F}\bigl(P_{φ,t}(\cdot \mid s,a), \hat P_t(\cdot \mid φ(s),a)\bigr)
  \le \hat δ_t\bigl(φ(s),a\bigr)
$$
for all $(s,a)$ (for example, take $\hat δ_t(\hat s,a)$ to be the supremum of the IPM distance over the fiber $φ^{-1}(\hat s)$).

We also restrict the value bounds to be $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$-measurable: $α^\pm_t = \hat α^\pm_t \circ φ$ and $β^\pm_t = \hat β^\pm_t \circ φ$ for some $\hat α^\pm_t \colon \hat {\ALPHABET S} \to \reals$ and $\hat β^\pm_t \in \hat {\ALPHABET Q}$. For any such $\hat α$, the IPM inequality between $P_{φ,t}$ and $\hat P_t$ gives
$$
  (\hat \DYNAMICS_t \hat α) \circ φ
  - (\hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat α)) \circ φ
  \le \DYNAMICS_t(\hat α \circ φ)
  \le (\hat \DYNAMICS_t \hat α) \circ φ
  + (\hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat α)) \circ φ.
$$
Applying this to $\hat α = \hat V^\star_{t+1}$ and using the definition of $\hat \MISMATCH_t$ bounds the mismatch by quantities on $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$:
$$
  (\hat ε^{-}_t - \hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})) \circ φ
  \le \hat \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}
  \le (\hat ε^{+}_t + \hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})) \circ φ.
$$

Combining these estimates, the recursions of @thm-signed-sample-path-abstract are implied by the $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$-side inequalities
\begin{align*}
  \hat β^-_t
  &\le \hat ε^{-}_t - \hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})
  + \hat \DYNAMICS_t \hat α^-_{t+1}
  - \hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat α^-_{t+1}),
  \\
  α^-_t
  &\le \ALPHABET T^{π^\star_t} β^-_t
\end{align*}
(or a minimum of $β^-_t(s,\cdot)$ over a candidate set containing $π^\star_t(s)$), and
\begin{align*}
  \hat β^+_t
  &\ge \hat ε^{+}_t + \hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat V^\star_{t+1})
  + \hat \DYNAMICS_t \hat α^+_{t+1}
  + \hat δ_t\, ρ_{\F}(\hat α^+_{t+1}),
  \\
  \hat α^+_t
  &\ge \ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} \hat β^+_t.
\end{align*}
Lifting via $α^\pm_t = \hat α^\pm_t \circ φ$ and $β^\pm_t = \hat β^\pm_t \circ φ$ (and using $\ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t \circ φ}( \hat β^+_t \circ φ) = (\ALPHABET T^{\hat π^\star_t} \hat β^+_t)\circ φ$) yields valid bounds for @thm-signed-sample-path-abstract. The entire recursion is thus computable from the approximate model together with the $\hat {\ALPHABET S}$-measurable discrepancies $(\hat ε^\pm_t, \hat δ_t)$.
